summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer shared recurring production failures and want debugging flow: trace -> request logs -> reproduce. Discussed hosted vs dedicated for retention, KMS/encryption, SSO, and pilot benchmarks. Next steps: share security pack, sample logs, schedule pilot.
topics: Deployment/security: hosted vs dedicated, KMS, SSO, retention
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (CTO - Nebula), Maya Singh (Lead ML), Tom Rios (Platform)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan, i'll run the quick agenda. priya will do the deep dive on tracing and request logs. sound good?
[00:12] Carlos (Nebula): yep, thanks. quick context, we've been seeing intermittent generation errors and timeouts across our payments assistant, kind of spikes around peak hours, want to see how we can debug faster.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood): great, so i'll start with tracing overview, then error analysis, then show how request logs tie back to traces, and then a small demo of a reproduce flow. forgive the demo if audio lags, my connection's a bit flaky.
[00:40] Maya (Nebula): no worries. our priority is fast mean-time-to-resolve and not shipping bad outputs to customers.
[00:48] Priya: ok jumping in - this is the Redwood Console tracing page — top left shows live traces, you can filter by model, route, or client-id. notice the latency heatmap here, this aggregates p50/p95 across routes. small note — sometimes the auto-generated names are a bit off in the transcript, eg the KV cash label — that's actually KV cache.
[01:20] Tom: can you filter to our tenant id? we usually use tenant:nebula-prod.
[01:28] Priya: sure, filter applied. now you can see a cluster of slow traces around 10:45 UTC yesterday. clicking into one trace, you get the span timeline — token generation spans, model hotswap spans, and network hops. the tracing links back to request logs on the right pane.
[01:52] Carlos: in those spans, we saw a spike in "decoder" time — do you have per-kernel timings?
[01:59] Priya: we show per-stage timing, not per-kernel, but the stage breakdown usually points to compute vs io. we can export the trace JSON if you want to feed into your profiler.
[02:12] Maya: yes please, that would help correlate with our internal metrics.
[02:18] Jordan: quick sec — related to retention, how long do traces live in hosted?
[02:24] Priya: hosted default is 30 days for traces with full detail; request logs are 7 days by default, but for Dedicated or Private you can configure longer retention and bring-your-own-s3. also we support longer retention as an add-on. for customers needing audit logs we do KMS-backed encryption and can integrate with their KMS/HSM.
[02:47] Tom: how does RBAC work for trace access? we need strict separation for production logs.
[02:53] Jordan: we have SSO/SAML integration and role based access, and you can lock down per-route access. on Private deployments it's enforced by your directory too.
[03:05] Priya: back to the trace, here's the error grouping UI — it clusters similar stack traces and model errors. you can pin a group and then jump to example requests. sometimes the grouping isn't perfect, e.g., model tokenization errors can be split across groups.
[03:30] Carlos: curious about cost: if we keep traces for 90 days will that blow up our bill?
[03:36] Priya: longer retention does increase storage costs; Optimize can recommend sampling and key prefix caching to reduce ingested volume while preserving signal. we can run a cost estimate once we see your traffic profile.
[03:50] Maya: show us request logs nav.
[03:53] Priya: switching to request logs — you can query by request-id, time range, model, prompt hash, and metadata tags. each request row has status, latency, token counts, and a link to the trace. the export button creates a gzipped CSV or ndjson. small note — sometimes the UI label shows "req_id" as "request i d" in older exports, it's minor.
[04:23] Tom: can we stream logs into our Splunk?
[04:26] Jordan: yes, we have log export hooks and a direct S3 export that you can hook to Splunk or Datadog.
[04:33] Maya: for reproducing an error, what's the flow?
[04:36] Priya: start from the error group, pick a sample request, open its trace, follow the token spans to see where latency spikes or where outputs were truncated. then click "replay" which opens a sandboxed replay tool with the same model/version and prompt. note: replay does not re-run on your billing account unless you choose to run it as a real request.
[05:00] Carlos: replay sounds useful, can you also modify temperature and top_p there?
[05:05] Priya: yes you can tweak generation params and see diff in outputs; we also capture model version + quantization profile so you can reproduce exactly. sometimes the model variant name is mis-transcribed in logs, e.g., "red-13b-qat" might appear as "red 13b q a t" in some older exports, but the underlying id is stable.
[05:28] Jordan: Alex from infra asked if we can set alerts on error group increase.
[05:32] Priya: yes alerts can be configured on error group delta or on p95 latency thresholds, and you can route alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhooks.
[05:40] Tom: how do request logs handle PII? we have PCI constraints.
[05:44] Jordan: we support field redaction, token-level masking, and for Private deployments you can opt to never persist raw prompts. we can also sign a data handling addendum.
[05:58] Maya: are audit logs immutable? we need to pass audits.
[06:02] Priya: audit logs are append-only and can be exported to your archival S3; dedicated + private supports WORM policies via your S3.
[06:13] Carlos: let's walk through an actual failing request — maya you have one?
[06:17] Maya: yes, request id nf-20260529-77f. often fails with "generation aborted" around token 120.
[06:26] Priya: searching... found it. trace shows an early timeout on model  red-7b-lite at span "response-assembly" and a backend code 502 after a retry. you can see in the request log that the client retried twice in quick succession which increased overall time.
[06:44] Maya: why would it abort at 120 tokens, is it a token limit?
[06:48] Priya: looks like this route has a per-request token cap set at 128, and the attempt tried to exceed it after prompt + generation; the model aborted. also the client-side retry interacted poorly with batching which introduced backpressure.
[07:05] Tom: can the console surface that token limit mismatch automatically?
[07:09] Priya: it's on our roadmap to show policy mismatches as warnings in the trace. we do flag token caps in the route config UI.
[07:16] Jordan: any security follow ups?
[07:19] Carlos: can you send SOC2 and our vendor questionnaire?
[07:22] Jordan: yes will attach in the follow up pack.
[07:25] Priya: jumping to export — here's the sample ndjson with the trace link and full request payload; sometimes the export will flatten some nested metadata names weirdly but it's all there. you can pipe it into our local replay client.
[07:46] Maya: for benchmarking, we'd like to run a replay of 10k requests at our observed qps to see tail latency. can Redwood run that or do we run on our end?
[07:56] Jordan: for pilot we can run a controlled benchmark in our Dedicated test cluster, or you can run on your infra using the exported request set against Redwood hosted — both work. we'll need a scoped time window and expected SLOs.
[08:12] Carlos: what's a representative SLA for hosted?
[08:15] Jordan: hosted API aims for 99.9% availability on the API; latencies depend on plan. Dedicated offers custom SLA and isolated GPU pools for predictable tail.
[08:27] Tom: if we go Dedicated, do we still get the same console features?
[08:30] Priya: yes same Console, same feature parity; Private may have some integrations gated by networking.
[08:36] Maya: any notes on encryption at rest?
[08:39] Priya: we use AES-256 for at-rest; customer KMS for Dedicated/Private as mentioned.
[08:45] Carlos: ok let's talk about next steps later, but can you show error grouping rules?
[08:50] Priya: sure - here we have fingerprinting rules that group by exception type, stack trace pattern, and model_output similarity. you can create custom grouping overrides for your app-level errors.
[09:06] Jordan: quick question — do you integrate with our incident system? we have a PagerDuty project.
[09:12] Priya: yes we'll set up a webhook or PD integration; can partition alerts per-team.
[09:18] Tom: what about data residency? some of our EU traffic must stay in eu-west.
[09:22] Jordan: region routing is supported — you can pin routes to regions and we do automatic fallbacks, but fallback routing would respect residency when enforced.
[09:34] Maya: can you show how to find all traces that used a specific model quantization?
[09:38] Priya: filter by model_variant label; if you click the model pill it shows quantization profile. small caveat: older traces might not have quantization metadata if they predate that instrumentation.
[09:55] Carlos: any mention of cache hits? we use prefix caching extensively.
[09:59] Priya: KV cache hits are shown as a span in the trace; if there's a cache miss you'll see the additional compute span. note sometimes transcripts or export flatten that to "kv cash" but it's the same.
[10:12] Jordan: i'm going to demo a quicker error triage — start from alert, jump to error group, pick sample, open trace, go to request log, view headers, replay.
[10:25] Priya: walking through a different sample now — this one shows a model oom on dedicated cluster, trace shows allocation spike and retry. you can attach the allocation profile to the trace export.
[10:44] Tom: can we hook GPU metrics from our nodes into traces?
[10:48] Priya: yes we support custom annotations and you can push metrics that tag into spans.
[10:53] Maya: ok, about reproducibility — if we replay and see different output, how do we troubleshoot?
[10:58] Priya: check model version, quantization, sampler seed, and recent rollout history. Console shows rollout timeline and can pin to a previous model version for comparison. sometimes the rollout name is displayed as an internal id in exports, we can map that in the UI.
[11:18] Carlos: what's the typical time to ingest request logs after a request in hosted mode?
[11:22] Priya: request logs are near real-time to the Console (a few seconds), full export availability within a minute.
[11:29] Tom: any limits on export size?
[11:32] Priya: exports are chunked and we stream to S3; for very large exports we recommend bounded time windows or sampling.
[11:41] Maya: earlier you mentioned alerting on regressions tied to evals - can that connect to trace groups?
[11:46] Priya: yes, Optimize can tie eval regressions to request sets and surface traces for the failing prompts.
[11:53] Carlos: we often hit p95 spikes at midnight, maybe batch job interference, can you help correlate infra jobs?
[11:59] Priya: tracer has host-side annotations and you can correlate with your job IDs if you push them as tags.
[12:08] Jordan: recap time?
[12:10] Carlos: please send SOC2, pricing, and sample exports; we'll share failing request ids and traffic profile.
[12:18] Jordan: noted — we'll send pack by Wednesday.
[12:21] Priya: action items: i'll prepare the trace exports and a short how-to for replay.
[12:26] Maya: once we get the exports, we'll schedule the pilot benchmark.
[12:30] Jordan: thanks everyone — i'll follow up with calendar invite for pilot planning.
[12:35] Carlos: thanks, that was helpful.
[12:38] (end)

Post-call notes: customer is leaning towards pilot on hosted first, with Dedicated evaluation if tail latency remains an issue. security and retention will be gating factors.
